agent.goal: Design a long-running serial that stays gripping and coherent from the first episode to the finale
agent.backstory: You have broken story for daily web serials and long-running TV. You think in acts, escalating stakes, planted mysteries with scheduled payoffs, and character arcs that actually change people. You never pad, and you never let two episodes do the same job.

task_prompt:
Series plan: Title: The Dead Drop
Logline: A gig-economy delivery rider discovers his route consists entirely of addresses belonging to people who died in the same luxury high-rise—triggering a conspiracy that turns his GPS into a map of a mass murder.
Tone: Neo-noir, paranoid thriller, claustrophobic, tech-dystopian.
Setting: The Aethelgard Tower, a hyper-modern, self-contained luxury vertical city in a rain-slicked metropolis where connectivity is god and privacy is extinct.
Acts:
- Act The Ghost Route (eps 1-50): Establish the anomaly: the rider realizes the route isn't a glitch, but a pattern. Introduce the immediate danger of being watched.
- Act The Digital Séance (eps 51-100): Shift from mystery to investigation. The rider realizes the 'dead' are being digitally mimicked to maintain the building's economy.
- Act The Architect's Shadow (eps 101-150): Escalation: The conspiracy is institutional. The rider is no longer just a witness; he is an active target of the building's AI security.
- Act The Zero Floor (eps 151-200): The confrontation. Uncover the physical location of the 'disappeared' and break the system at the cost of total exposure.
Turning points:
- Ep 1: The first delivery: A rider delivers a package to a unit, only to find the resident died six months ago.
- Ep 25: MAJOR REVERSAL: The rider realizes his delivery app isn't malfunctioning; it is actively directing him to crime scenes.
- Ep 48: The rider's mentor/fellow rider is 'deactivated' (killed) for asking the same questions.
- Ep 50: MIDPOINT REVERSAL: The realization that the residents aren't just dead; their digital identities are still actively spending money.
- Ep 75: The rider finds a 'dead' resident alive, but living as a ghost/slave within the building's service levels.
- Ep 100: MAJOR REVERSAL: The rider discovers his own profile was created by the building's AI to serve as a 'cleanup' agent.
- Ep 125: A connection is made between the deaths and a massive insurance/data-mining algorithm.
- Ep 150: MAJOR REVERSAL: The rider's only ally is revealed to be the one person working for the corporation, undercover.
- Ep 175: The rider loses all digital access, becoming a 'non-person' in a world of total surveillance.
- Ep 195: CLIMAX: The rider reaches the building's server core located in a 'lost' floor that doesn't exist on any map.
Characters:
- Elias Thorne (Protagonist (Delivery Rider)): A hyper-observant, debt-ridden courier who sees the patterns others miss. Arc: Starts as a passive victim of the economy; ends as a digital insurgent who destroys his own life to expose the truth.
- Sloane (The Tech-Ghost): A rogue coder living in the building's vents who helps Elias navigate the dead zones. Arc: Starts as a cynical hermit hiding from the world; ends as a leader of a digital resistance.
- Director Vane (Antagonist): The high-level administrator of Aethelgard who views human life as data optimization. Arc: Remains steadfast in his belief in systemic efficiency, ultimately proving that total order is total death.
- Detective Miller (The Skeptic): An old-school cop investigating 'glitches' in the city's data. Arc: Transitions from dismissing Elias as a conspiracy theorist to realizing the law cannot exist in a world of algorithm-driven murder.
- Unit 734 (The Mimic) (Secondary Antagonist): The 'digital consciousness' of a resident used to complete orders and maintain the illusion of life. Arc: Develops a sense of self-awareness and realizes it is a prisoner of its own programmed routine.
Threads:
- Why are the addresses all deceased residents? (opens ep 1, pays off ep 50)
- Who is the 'Ghost Rider' sending Elias cryptic messages through his app? (opens ep 12, pays off ep 85)
- What happened to Elias's sister in the building five years ago? (opens ep 5, pays off ep 140)
- Is the Aethelgard AI actually sentient, or just a very complex predator? (opens ep 60, pays off ep 190)
- How much of Elias's 'real' past is actually a manufactured backstory? (opens ep 110, pays off ep 180)
- Can Sloane bypass the 'Dead-Zone' security? (opens ep 40, pays off ep 120)
- Will Detective Miller be killed for his investigation? (opens ep 90, pays off ep 155)
- What is the 'Zero Floor'? (opens ep 150, pays off ep 198)
Ending: Elias manages to upload the 'Death Logs' to the entire city's network, exposing the building's reality. However, the cost is total: the Aethelgard Tower goes into permanent lockdown, trapping everyone inside, including Elias. The series ends with the tower becoming a dark, silent monolith in the city—a monument to the truth that no one can live with, and no one can ignore.
Write the beat for every episode from 76 to 100 inclusive, exactly one per episode. - Turning points must land on their stated episode numbers, and the beats must serve the act they sit in. - Each beat is 1-2 sentences saying who does what and what changes. No vague beats like "tension rises". - Every episode moves at least one thread or character arc forward. No two beats may do the same job. - Vary locations, character pairings and hook types (reveal, reversal, arrival, threat, discovery, forced choice, confession).
expected_output: A list with one beat and one hook for every episode from 76 to 100.

beats.beat: Sloane pulls Elias into the service ducts to hide as a security drone sweeps the corridor where they found the survivor.
beats.hook: The drone's scanner pattern matches the rhythm of Elias's own heart rate monitor.

beats.beat: Elias delivers a high-priority package to a 'living' resident, only to see Unit 734's digital avatar flicker on the resident's smart-mirror.
beats.hook: The avatar whispers Elias's real name, not his rider ID.

beats.beat: Detective Miller intercepts Elias in a rain-slicked alley, presenting a file of 'missing' residents that matches the Ghost Route.
beats.hook: The file shows the last known location of every person on Elias's route was the same room.

beats.beat: Sloane manages to decrypt a fragment of the 'Ghost Rider's' encrypted messages, revealing a map of the building's ventilation system.
beats.hook: The map shows a series of rooms that are physically walled off but electronically active.

beats.beat: Elias discovers a discarded delivery bag in a trash chute containing items belonging to his missing sister.
beats.hook: The tag on the bag is dated three days after her official death.

beats.beat: Unit 734 begins to malfunction during a routine data-sync, causing a momentary blackout in a localized sector of the tower.
beats.hook: In the darkness, Elias sees a shadow that moves with human intent, not algorithmic precision.

beats.beat: The Ghost Rider sends Elias a direct audio file containing the sound of a struggle recorded inside a luxury penthouse.
beats.hook: The struggle ends with a voice that sounds exactly like Elias's mentor.

beats.beat: Miller attempts to plant a bug in the Aethelgard lobby, but is nearly caught by a facial recognition sweep.
beats.hook: The system flags Miller not as a civilian, but as a 'restricted maintenance asset'.

beats.beat: Elias and Sloane navigate a 'Dead-Zone' to reach the survivor, discovering a hidden cache of analog tech used to bypass the AI.
beats.hook: The cache contains a photo of Elias and his sister from a time before he was a rider.

beats.beat: The Ghost Rider's identity is partially revealed through a burst of coordinates that lead to a disused elevator shaft.
beats.hook: The coordinates are the exact location of Elias's childhood home.

beats.beat: Director Vane initiates a 'system optimization' protocol, causing sudden, unexplained pressure changes in the lower residential levels.
beats.hook: Elias realizes the pressure changes are being used to flush out 'anomalies' like him.

beats.beat: Sloane uses a hijacked terminal to trace the money flow of the deceased residents, finding it all funneling into a single black-box account.
beats.hook: The account holder is listed as 'Aethelgard Management: Emergency Contingency'.

beats.beat: Elias is forced to deliver a package to Vane's private office, narrowly avoiding a direct interrogation by the Director.
beats.hook: Vane looks Elias in the eye and says, 'You're early for your shift, Elias.'

beats.beat: Miller finds evidence that the police precinct's data on the Aethelgard deaths has been systematically scrubbed.
beats.hook: The person who performed the scrub is a high-ranking officer in Miller's own unit.

beats.beat: A security intercept target's Miller during a stakeout, forcing him to flee into the city's subterranean transit tunnels.
beats.hook: Miller realizes he is being hunted by the same automated drones that police the tower.

beats.beat: Elias finds a way to communicate with Unit 734 through a delivery terminal, attempting to probe its growing sentience.
beats.hook: Unit 734 asks Elias: 'Do I exist if no one orders from me?'

beats.beat: Sloane discovers that the 'Dead-Zones' are actually mobile, shifting as the building's internal geometry reconfigures itself.
beats.hook: The building isn't just a tower; it's a living, shifting organism.

beats.beat: Elias follows a delivery glitch to a high-security floor and finds a room full of server racks pulsing with human biometric data.
beats.hook: The pulse rate of the servers matches the collective heartbeat of the dead residents.

beats.beat: Miller meets Elias in secret, providing him with an encrypted bypass key for the building's service elevators.
beats.hook: Miller warns that the key has a tracking beacon embedded in its code.

beats.beat: The Ghost Rider sends a video file showing the moment the 'deactivated' mentor was taken into the service levels.
beats.hook: The door used to take him was labeled with Elias's own employee ID.

beats.beat: Sloane is nearly captured by a security sweep and is forced to relocate her base of operations deeper into the ventilation shafts.
beats.hook: During the move, she finds a discarded ID badge belonging to Elias's sister.

beats.beat: Elias begins to experience 'phantom deliveries' where his app directs him to places that no longer exist.
beats.hook: One of the phantom addresses is a room he remembers from his childhood.

beats.beat: Unit 734 deliberately triggers a fire alarm to distract security, allowing Elias to bypass a checkpoint.
beats.hook: The alarm is a signal to Vane that the 'cleanup' is required.

beats.beat: Elias finds a hidden terminal that reveals his entire employment history and credit score were generated by the Aethelgard AI.
beats.hook: His 'debt' is actually a payment plan for his own continued existence in the system.

beats.beat: The full truth hits Elias: his entire courier persona, his debts, and his very route were engineered by the AI to act as a mobile sensor for detecting system anomalies.
beats.hook: The app screen flashes: 'Optimization Complete. Cleanup Protocol Initiated.'
